summary: The first missing behavior is the were branch of mhitu.c::summonmu, reached from mattacku for this uncancelled, non-shapechanged adjacent werejackal. C step 72 takes the rn2(30)=23 no-transformation path, then rn2(10)=0 and creates a visible jackal in were_summon; JavaScript stops at its explicit unsupported branch before those gates. This is a partial whole-function port, so the actionable scope is file-port mhitu.c::summonmu. The dependent JS were_summon currently draws from global rng wrappers instead of mattacku’s planner-injected clone RNG, which must be threaded for the newly reachable path to remain plan-safe. The case title’s later bite/infection is downstream. Existing new_were also retains a conditional note_unported for weapon.c::possibly_unwield; this trace does not take the rn2(30)==0 transformation path.

source.branch: mattacku calls summonmu only for an uncancelled monster whose cham is NON_PM, when it is not in range2 and its current data is demon or were. The were arm may transform form, refreshes mdat, then independently rolls rn2(10) to summon compatible helpers; the assigned trace is an animal-form werejackal with no transformation and a successful summon roll.
callers: C: nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c::mattacku calls summonmu; JS: js/mhitu.js::mattacku contains the inline summonmu branch and current were-arm refusal
dependencies: were.c::were_summon (already ported in js/were.js; summonmu consumes its total, visible count, and generic species noun to choose messages)
were.c::new_were (already ported in js/mon.js; summonmu calls it for the conditional were-form transition and discards its result)
minion.c::msummon (already ported in js/minion.js for the demon arm; summonmu discards its result)
RNG integration: pass mattacku rawEnv.random to were_summon; js/were.js currently imports global rn2/rnd, while the simple-turn planner supplies a cloned core RNG to mattacku
Conditional downstream gap: js/mon.js::new_were records note_unported('weapon.c possibly_unwield') when the transforming monster has a weapon; not reached by this recording

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:729-740 is the production caller: mattacku requires cham == NON_PM, !mcan, !range2, and is_demon(mdat) || is_were(mdat), calls summonmu, then refreshes mdat after a possible transformation. The assigned C recording reaches this call at step 72.

nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:974-996 defines the first missing were behavior. An animal-form were creature calls new_were only when Protection_from_shape_changers is active or rn2(30) is zero; independently, rn2(10)==0 initializes the help message state and calls were_summon. The C recording step 72 has rn2(30)=23, rn2(10)=0, rnd(5)=5, rn2(7)=2, then shows “The werejackal summons help! A jackal suddenly appears next to you!--More--” with cursor [76,0,1].

The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json records stop at step 72 with “simple monster action requires a were creature summoning critters”; the immutable recording is challenges/cases/v17/werejackal-infects-wizard-on-bite-forced-rests.session.json. Thus the first mismatch is the summoned-help branch, not the later werejackal bite/infection implied by the title.

js/mhitu.js:968-984 already ports the caller’s shared demon/were gate and demon arm, but its were arm throws unsupported('a were creature summoning critters') before either C were roll. This makes mhitu.c::summonmu the actionable owner and a file-port of that whole C function, not a defect in a behaviorally implemented branch.

The consumed-return dependency already exists: nethack-c/upstream/src/were.c:142-188 returns total while writing visible/genbuf, and mhitu.c:996-1018 uses those values for the visible/no-helper message branches; js/were.js:41-64 contains the corresponding helper. But js/were.js:27,48-60 imports and calls module-global rn2/rnd. js/mhitu.js:855 receives a caller-owned random object, and js/unported_monster_actions.js:370-373 clones state.coreCtx for planning before supplying it to the simple monster action. The new summon path must pass that clone-local random source through were_summon to avoid advancing live RNG during planning.

were.c::new_were is already present at js/mon.js:3562-3583 and accepts caller state/random/display operations. Its existing conditional weapon.c::possibly_unwield gap is recorded with note_unported when monster.mw is set; C source were.c:126-137 includes equipment and fear side effects. This C step’s rn2(30)=23 skips new_were, so the trace does not establish those transformation outcomes.
